Here’s a 4-day, 20–30 min weekly pool plan at Blue Lagoon’s 50 m pool that builds steady endurance while staying shoulder-friendly. It uses short repeats, lots of easy aerobic work, and kick/balance drills to reduce shoulder load. Use generous rests (20–30 seconds) and keep everything pain-free.

Day 1 – Aerobic 50s
- Pre-pool (dryland bands, 3–5 min): light external rotations and scap squeezes.
- Warm-up: 4 x 50 easy freestyle, include 2 x 50 as 25 kick + 25 swim.
- Drill: 2 x 50 side-kick with body rotation (switch sides at 25).
- Main: 8 x 50 freestyle easy-moderate, 20–30s rest. Focus on smooth, relaxed strokes.
- Cooldown: 2 x 50 very easy swim or kick.

Day 2 – Kick-supported endurance
- Warm-up: 2 x 50 easy swim + 2 x 50 easy kick (on back or with board if available).
- Drill: 4 x 25 6-kick switch (side-kick, 6 kicks, rotate).
- Main: 6 x 100 as 75 easy swim + 25 kick, 30s rest. Keep form pristine.
- Cooldown: 2 x 50 easy.

Day 3 – Continuous aerobic mix (variety to reduce boredom)
- Warm-up: 3 x 50 easy swim, 2 x 50 kick.
- Main (10–15 min continuous, smooth): repeat 50 easy swim + 25 kick + 25 drill (side-kick or fingertip-drag if painless).
- Cooldown: 2 x 50 easy.

Day 4 – Gentle ladder
- Warm-up: 4 x 50 easy.
- Main: 50–100–150–100–50, 20–30s rest between. All at conversational effort. If shoulder twinges, cap the longest rep at 100.
- Optional top-up: 4 x 50 easy aerobic, 20s rest.
- Cooldown: 2 x 50 easy.

Weekly progression (pick 1–2 tweaks each week):
- Add 1–2 x 50 to Day 1.
- Add 1 x 100 to Day 2 (or make 2 of the 100s “negative split”).
- Add 2–3 minutes to Day 3’s continuous block.
- On Day 4, add a second ladder only if pain-free.

Shoulder-safe cues
- No paddles, no sprints, no butterfly. Keep stroke relaxed, short, and symmetrical.
- Soft hand entry in line with shoulder, roll from the hips, keep elbows below shoulder height if you fatigue.
- If discomfort >2/10, switch to kick or drills, or stop.

Asthma note
- Take a long, easy warm-up and rest as needed. Keep your nebulizer handy poolside and adjust rests if breathing feels off.
